fullPassage:
The Magic of Morning Pages

Welcome to my channel Good Habits! This is Regan, your podcast host. Today, I'm going to talk about a way of starting the day that many people, including me, find enormously useful. It's a kind of journaling called "the morning pages." There is no age at which it is too late to form this habit. I started eight years ago as a high school student, and that's why today's episode is especially for my teenage subscribers.

The morning pages are three pages of "free writing," ideally done first thing in the morning. The concept is simple. Get up every morning, pick up a pen and a notebook, and write whatever crosses your mind until you have filled three pages. The technique was originally developed to help writers and artists overcome a loss of creativity, but anybody can use it to create a better life.

There is no right or wrong way to write your morning pages, but there are two rules. First, don't judge your writing as good or bad. These pages are meant to be a "brain cleansing," so don't worry about writing correctly. Second, keep your writing completely private. It is important for you to write freely and honestly. You're even advised not to read your writing yourself for weeks.

Now, let me share the experiences of some people I interviewed. David, a chef and kitchen manager, who has been writing morning pages for two years, says:

My job tends to be very stressful. When I started writing morning pages, I just wrote a lot of complaints about my hard life. Later, I began to ask questions, like "What would make my life easier today?" "How can I improve my recipes?" Sometimes, I keep asking questions until I reach a sort of "click moment." It feels like a door opening to great ideas. Nowadays, I feel less stressed, enjoy my job more, and am more productive.

Now, let's listen to Yuna, a high school junior:

When I started this exercise last year, I simply wrote random thoughts like this:
I'm sleepy. A slight headache's starting.
I need to finish the math assignment today …
I don't know what more to write now.

But soon I found I had deeper and deeper thoughts. Now, I normally start by writing about today's tasks or worries. After that, I write about my dreams and how to move towards them. I often come up with great plans and a clear sense of purpose to start the day. Most importantly, I'm much happier than before.

I can totally relate to these two people because their experiences are similar to mine. Like Yuna, I started this journaling during my first year of high school. At that time, I felt lost, stressed, and unsure about the future, and it wasn't easy for me to concentrate. When I first tried writing three daily pages, I didn't expect to stick to it. But I did, and it changed my life!

Releasing my feelings onto paper every morning helped relieve my emotional tension. I gained more inner peace, which improved my schoolwork performance. Like David, I asked many questions, for instance, "Why was I so angry yesterday?" "Why are things less fun these days?" Then, I started raising more challenging ones: "What could make me happier right now?" "What is my ideal future? Can I reach it? How?"

Answering these questions showed me what kind of person I was and what my needs, values, passions, and talents were. More importantly, I came to know what I truly wanted! I remembered my childhood dreams of being a writer, songwriter, and radio host. Gradually, vague ideas became clear plans. Years later, here I am, a successful podcaster and vlogger! I've also published a book and a music album. My morning pages, which I still write every day, have given me the drive and ideas to achieve these aims.

Dear subscribers, will you try writing your morning pages, too? You never know what creative energy or ideas you have until you start exploring. Don't be a perfectionist, though. If you miss a few days, simply open your notebook and start again! The ultimate aim is to improve your mental health and help you lead a happier, more creative life.

questions.passage: The morning pages are three pages of "free writing," (A)[ideally / rarely] done first thing in the morning. The concept is simple. Get up every morning, pick up a pen and a notebook, and write whatever (B)[crosses / leaves] your mind until you have filled three pages. The technique was originally developed to help writers and artists (C)[overcome / maintain] a loss of creativity, but anybody can use it to create a better life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 모닝페이지는 세 쪽짜리 자유 글쓰기로, 이상적으로 아침에 가장 먼저 하는 것이다. 마음에 떠오르는 것은 무엇이든 세 페이지를 채울 때까지 쓴다. 이 기법은 원래 작가와 예술가들이 창의력 상실을 극복하도록 돕기 위해 개발되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ideally — crosses — overcome
❌ ② rarely — crosses — maintain
❌ ③ ideally — leaves — maintain
❌ ④ rarely — leaves — overcome
✅ (A) ideally: '이상적으로' 아침 첫 번째로 하면 좋다는 의미. rarely(거의 ~않다)는 권장 의미와 반대. ✅ (B) crosses: 'crosses your mind'는 '마음에 떠오르다'라는 관용표현. leaves(떠나다)는 반대 의미. ✅ (C) overcome: '극복하다'. maintain(유지하다)은 창의력 상실을 유지한다는 뜻이 되어 부적절.
det.tip: cross one's mind = '~의 마음에 떠오르다'. overcome = '극복하다' (over + come). ideally = '이상적으로'.

questions.passage: When I started writing morning pages, I just wrote a lot of (A)[complaints / compliments] about my hard life. Later, I began to ask questions. Sometimes, I keep asking questions until I reach a sort of 'click moment.' Nowadays, I feel less stressed, enjoy my job more, and am more (B)[productive / destructive]. I can totally (C)[relate / object] to these two people because their experiences are similar to mine.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 모닝페이지를 쓰기 시작했을 때 힘든 삶에 대한 불평을 많이 적었다. 요즘은 스트레스가 덜하고 더 생산적이다. 이 두 사람의 경험이 비슷해서 전적으로 공감할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① compliments — productive — relate
❌ ② complaints — destructive — object
✅ ③ complaints — productive — relate
❌ ④ compliments — destructive — object
✅ (A) complaints: 힘든 삶에 대한 '불평'. compliments(칭찬)는 hard life와 어울리지 않음. ✅ (B) productive: '생산적인'. destructive(파괴적인)는 긍정적 변화 맥락과 반대. ✅ (C) relate: 'relate to'는 '공감하다'. object(반대하다)는 유사한 경험에 대한 반응으로 부적절.
det.tip: complaint(불평) vs compliment(칭찬): 철자 유사하나 의미 반대. relate to = '~에 공감하다'.

questions.passage: At that time, I felt lost, stressed, and unsure about the future, and it wasn't easy for me to (A)[concentrate / cooperate]. Releasing my feelings onto paper every morning helped relieve my emotional tension. I gained more inner peace, which improved my schoolwork (B)[performance / attendance]. Gradually, (C)[vague / vivid] ideas became clear plans. Years later, here I am, a successful podcaster and vlogger!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 당시 길을 잃은 느낌이었고 집중하기 쉽지 않았다. 내적 평화를 얻어 학업 성적이 향상되었다. 막연한 아이디어들이 점차 명확한 계획이 되었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① cooperate — performance — vague
✅ ② concentrate — performance — vague
❌ ③ concentrate — attendance — vivid
❌ ④ cooperate — attendance — vivid
✅ (A) concentrate: '집중하다'. cooperate(협력하다)는 co-로 시작해 혼동 가능하나, 혼자 공부하는 맥락에서 부적절. ✅ (B) performance: 'schoolwork performance'는 '학업 성적'. attendance(출석)는 inner peace와 논리적 연결 약함. ✅ (C) vague: '막연한' 아이디어가 clear plans이 됨. vivid(생생한)는 이미 명확하므로 clear과 대조 불가.
det.tip: concentrate(집중하다) vs cooperate(협력하다): 접두사 con-(함께)과 co-(함께)로 혼동 주의. vague(막연한) ↔ clear(명확한).

questions.passage: There is no right or wrong way to write your morning pages, but there are two rules. First, don't ①<u>judge</u> your writing as good or bad. These pages are meant to be a 'brain cleansing,' so don't worry about writing ②<u>correctly</u>. Second, keep your writing completely ③<u>public</u>. It is important for you to write ④<u>freely</u> and honestly.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 모닝페이지를 쓰는 데 옳고 그른 방법은 없지만 두 가지 규칙이 있다. 첫째, 글이 좋다 나쁘다 ①판단하지 마라. 이 페이지들은 두뇌 정화용이니 ②올바르게 쓰는 것은 걱정하지 마라. 둘째, 글을 완전히 ③공개적으로 유지하라. ④자유롭게 솔직하게 쓰는 것이 중요하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① judge: 원문 그대로. 판단하지 말라는 맥락에 적절. ✅ ② correctly: 원문 그대로. 올바르게 쓰는 것을 걱정하지 말라. ❌ ③ public → private: 글을 '비공개'로 유지해야 자유롭게 쓸 수 있음. 공개(public)는 반대 의미. ✅ ④ freely: 원문 그대로. 자유롭게 솔직하게 쓰라.
det.tip: private(비공개의) ↔ public(공개의). 모닝페이지의 핵심 규칙은 비공개 유지.

questions.passage: My job tends to be very ①<u>stressful</u>. When I started writing morning pages, I just wrote a lot of complaints about my hard life. Later, I began to ask questions. Sometimes, I keep asking questions until I reach a sort of "click moment." It feels like a door opening to great ideas. Nowadays, I feel less stressed, enjoy my job more, and am more ②<u>productive</u>. But soon I found I had ③<u>deeper</u> and deeper thoughts. I often come up with great plans and a clear sense of ④<u>confusion</u> to start the day.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 내 직업은 매우 ①스트레스가 많다. 요즘은 더 ②생산적이다. 점점 더 ③깊은 생각을 하게 되었다. 하루를 시작할 뚜렷한 ④혼란을 생각해 낸다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① stressful: 원문 그대로. 직업이 스트레스가 많다. ✅ ② productive: 원문 그대로. 더 생산적. ✅ ③ deeper: 원문 그대로. 더 깊은 생각. ❌ ④ confusion → purpose: 하루를 시작할 '목적의식'이 맞음. confusion(혼란)은 긍정적 변화 맥락과 반대.
det.tip: purpose(목적) ↔ confusion(혼란). 'a clear sense of purpose' = '뚜렷한 목적의식'.

questions.passage: I can totally relate to these two people because their experiences are ①<u>similar</u> to mine. At that time, I felt lost, stressed, and unsure about the future, and it wasn't easy for me to ②<u>concentrate</u>. Releasing my feelings onto paper every morning helped ③<u>intensify</u> my emotional tension. I gained more inner peace, which improved my schoolwork ④<u>performance</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 이 두 사람의 경험은 나와 ①비슷하다. 당시 ②집중하기 쉽지 않았다. 매일 아침 감정을 종이에 풀어놓는 것이 정서적 긴장을 ③강화하는 데 도움이 되었다. 내적 평화를 얻어 학업 ④성적이 향상되었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① similar: 원문 그대로. 경험이 비슷하다. ✅ ② concentrate: 원문 그대로. 집중하기 어려웠다. ❌ ③ intensify → relieve: 감정을 종이에 풀어놓는 것은 긴장을 '완화'(relieve)하는 것. intensify(강화하다)는 반대 의미. ✅ ④ performance: 원문 그대로. 학업 성적.
det.tip: relieve(완화하다) ↔ intensify(강화하다). emotional tension(정서적 긴장)을 relieve하는 것이 모닝페이지의 효과.

questions.passage: Welcome to my channel Good Habits! This is Regan, your podcast host. Today, I'm going to talk about a way of starting the day that many people find enormously useful. It's a kind of journaling called "the morning pages." There is no age at which it is too late to form this habit. I started eight years ago as a high school student, and that's why today's episode is especially for my teenage __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 습관을 8년 전 고등학생 때부터 시작했고, 그래서 오늘 에피소드는 특히 십 대 구독자들을 위한 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① subscribers
❌ ② instructors
❌ ③ competitors
❌ ④ volunteers
✅ subscribers: 팟캐스트 채널의 '구독자'. 십 대 청취자를 대상으로 한 에피소드. ❌ instructors(강사), competitors(경쟁자), volunteers(자원봉사자)는 팟캐스트 청취 대상으로 부적절.
det.tip: subscriber = 구독자. subscribe(구독하다) + -er. podcast host가 자신의 청취자를 부르는 표현.

questions.passage: The morning pages are three pages of "free writing," ideally done first thing in the morning. The concept is simple. Get up every morning, pick up a pen and a notebook, and write whatever crosses your mind until you have filled three pages. The technique was originally developed to help writers and artists overcome a loss of __________, but anybody can use it to create a better life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 기법은 원래 작가와 예술가들이 창의력 상실을 극복하도록 돕기 위해 개발되었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① curiosity
❌ ② popularity
❌ ③ authority
✅ ④ creativity
✅ creativity: 작가와 예술가에게 가장 중요한 것은 '창의력'. 그 상실을 극복하려는 기법. ❌ curiosity(호기심): 작가에게 중요하나 'overcome a loss of curiosity'는 부자연스러움. ❌ popularity(인기): 글쓰기 기법과 무관. ❌ authority(권위): 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: creativity(창의력) = creative(창의적인)의 명사형. 작가/예술가의 핵심 역량.

questions.passage: At that time, I felt lost, stressed, and unsure about the future, and it wasn't easy for me to concentrate. When I first tried writing three daily pages, I didn't expect to stick to it. But I did, and it changed my life! Releasing my feelings onto paper every morning helped relieve my emotional __________. I gained more inner peace, which improved my schoolwork performance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 매일 아침 감정을 종이에 풀어놓는 것이 정서적 긴장을 완화하는 데 도움이 되었다. 내적 평화를 더 많이 얻었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① extension
❌ ② intention
✅ ③ tension
❌ ④ attention
✅ tension: 'emotional tension'은 '정서적 긴장'. relieve(완화하다)와 자연스럽게 결합. ❌ extension(확장): relieve와 어울리지 않음. ❌ intention(의도): emotional intention은 부자연스러움. ❌ attention(주의): relieve attention은 비관용적.
det.tip: tension(긴장) — extension(확장) — intention(의도) — attention(주의): 모두 -tion으로 끝나 혼동 주의. relieve tension = '긴장을 완화하다'는 고정 표현.

questions.passage: Today, I'm going to talk about a way of starting the day that many people, including me, find <u>enormously</u> useful.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 enormously와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 많은 사람들이 엄청나게 유용하다고 생각하는 하루 시작법에 대해 이야기하겠다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① slightly
✅ ② hugely
❌ ③ barely
❌ ④ rarely
✅ hugely: '매우, 엄청나게'로 enormously와 동의어. ❌ slightly(약간): 반의어. ❌ barely(거의 ~않게): 반의어. ❌ rarely(드물게): 빈도 부사로 의미 다름.
det.tip: enormously = hugely = immensely = tremendously: 모두 '엄청나게, 대단히'라는 뜻.

questions.passage: When I first tried writing three daily pages, I didn't expect to <u>stick to</u> it. But I did, and it changed my life!
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 stick to와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 처음 매일 세 쪽 글쓰기를 시도했을 때 계속하게 되리라고 기대하지 않았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① keep up with
❌ ② get rid of
❌ ③ look down on
❌ ④ come up with
✅ keep up with: '계속하다, 따라가다'로 stick to(고수하다, 계속하다)와 유사. ❌ get rid of(제거하다): 반대 의미. ❌ look down on(무시하다): 무관. ❌ come up with(생각해내다): 의미 다름.
det.tip: stick to = '~을 고수하다, 계속하다'. keep up with = '~을 따라가다, 계속하다'.

questions.passage: Answering these questions showed me what kind of person I was and what my needs, values, passions, and talents were. Gradually, <u>vague</u> ideas became clear plans.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 vague와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 막연한 아이디어들이 차츰 명확한 계획이 되었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① obvious
❌ ② specific
❌ ③ detailed
✅ ④ unclear
✅ unclear: '불분명한'으로 vague(막연한)와 동의어. ❌ obvious(분명한): 반의어. ❌ specific(구체적인): 반의어. ❌ detailed(상세한): 반의어.
det.tip: vague(막연한) = unclear = ambiguous = fuzzy. 반의어: clear, specific, definite.

questions.passage: It is important for you to write freely and honestly. You're even advised not to read your writing yourself for weeks. Keep your writing completely <u>private</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 private와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 글을 완전히 비공개로 유지하라.
det.analysis:
✅ ① public
❌ ② personal
❌ ③ secret
❌ ④ hidden
✅ public: '공개적인'으로 private(비공개의)의 정확한 반의어. ❌ personal(개인적인): private와 유사한 의미. ❌ secret(비밀의): private와 유사한 의미. ❌ hidden(숨겨진): private와 유사한 의미.
det.tip: private(비공개의) ↔ public(공개적인). 나머지 선지는 모두 private와 비슷한 뜻이라 반의어가 아님.

questions.passage: Nowadays, I feel less stressed, enjoy my job more, and am more <u>productive</u>. It feels like a door opening to great ideas.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 productive와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 요즘은 스트레스가 덜하고 일도 더 즐기며 더 생산적이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① effective
❌ ② constructive
✅ ③ inefficient
❌ ④ active
✅ inefficient: '비효율적인'으로 productive(생산적인)의 반의어. ❌ effective(효과적인): productive와 유사. ❌ constructive(건설적인): productive와 유사. ❌ active(활동적인): productive와 유사한 긍정 뉘앙스.
det.tip: productive(생산적인) ↔ unproductive / inefficient(비효율적인). constructive와 effective는 유의어이므로 반의어가 아님.

questions.passage:
(A) I remembered my childhood dreams of being a writer, songwriter, and radio host. Gradually, vague ideas became clear plans. My morning pages, which I still write every day, have given me the <u>drive</u> and ideas to achieve these aims.

(B) My parents wanted to visit the coast for a family trip. We decided to <u>drive</u> to the beach on the weekend. The beautiful scenery along the way made the journey worthwhile.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 drive가 각 문장에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 나의 모닝페이지는 이런 목표를 달성하기 위한 추진력과 아이디어를 제공했다. (B) 우리는 주말에 해변까지 운전해 가기로 했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 운전 — (B) 추진력
✅ ② (A) 추진력 — (B) 운전하다
❌ ③ (A) 추진력 — (B) 몰아붙이다
❌ ④ (A) 여행 — (B) 운전하다
✅ (A) 추진력: 목표 달성을 위한 동기/원동력. 명사로서 '추진력'의 의미. ✅ (B) 운전하다: 해변까지 차를 몰고 가다. 동사로서 '운전하다'. ❌ (A)운전–(B)추진력은 의미가 뒤바뀜. ❌ 몰아붙이다는 (B)의 맥락과 불일치.
det.tip: drive: ① (명사) 추진력, 의욕 ② (동사) 운전하다 ③ (동사) 몰아붙이다. 문맥에 따라 의미 구별.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a method or way of doing something, especially one that requires a special skill"

det.korean: "특별한 기술이 필요한, 무언가를 하는 방법이나 방식"
det.analysis:
❌ ① concept
❌ ② episode
❌ ③ complaint
✅ ④ technique
✅ technique: '기법, 기술'로 영영풀이에 정확히 부합. ❌ concept(개념): 추상적 생각이지 방법이 아님. ❌ episode(에피소드): 방송 회차. ❌ complaint(불평): 방법과 무관.
det.tip: technique = 기법, 기술. 본문에서 'The technique was originally developed to help writers...'로 사용됨.

questions.passage: Releasing my feelings onto paper every morning was helpful. I gained more inner peace, which improved my schoolwork __________. (perform)
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 매일 아침 감정을 종이에 풀어놓는 것이 도움이 되었다. 내적 평화를 얻어 학업 성적이 향상되었다.
det.analysis: ✅ performance: perform(수행하다) → performance(성과, 성적). 'improved my schoolwork ___'에서 명사가 필요. improved는 타동사로 목적어(명사)를 취함.
det.tip: perform(동사: 수행하다) → performance(명사: 수행, 성과). schoolwork performance = 학업 성적/성과.

questions.passage: The technique was originally developed to help writers and artists. Anybody can use it to lead a more __________ life. (create)
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 이 기법은 원래 작가와 예술가를 돕기 위해 개발되었다. 누구나 더 창의적인 삶을 영위하기 위해 사용할 수 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ creative: create(창조하다) → creative(창의적인). 'a more ___ life'에서 명사 life를 수식하는 형용사 필요.
det.tip: create(동사) → creative(형용사) → creativity(명사) → creatively(부사). 'more + 형용사 + 명사' 구조.

questions.passage: My job tends to be very stressful. When I started writing morning pages, I just wrote a lot of complaints about my hard life. Later, I began to ask questions, like "What would make my life easier today?" Sometimes, I keep asking questions until I reach a sort of "click moment." It feels like __________. Nowadays, I feel less stressed, enjoy my job more, and am more productive.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: a door opening to great ideas

det.korean: 계속 질문하다 '클릭 순간'에 도달하면 그것은 마치 멋진 아이디어들을 향한 문이 열리는 것처럼 느껴진다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① a wall blocking my progress
❌ ② a burden on my shoulders
✅ ③ a door opening to great ideas
❌ ④ a puzzle impossible to solve
✅ a door opening to great ideas: 'click moment' 후 아이디어가 떠오르는 긍정적 비유. 이후 스트레스가 줄고 생산적이 됨. ❌ a wall blocking: 부정적 이미지로 이후 긍정적 변화와 모순. ❌ a burden: 부정적. ❌ a puzzle impossible: 부정적.
det.tip: click moment = 깨달음의 순간. 이후 문맥이 긍정적(less stressed, more productive)이므로 긍정적 비유가 적절.

questions.passage: I can totally relate to these two people because their experiences are similar to mine. Answering deep questions showed me what kind of person I was and what my needs, values, passions, and talents were. More importantly, __________! I remembered my childhood dreams of being a writer, songwriter, and radio host. Gradually, vague ideas became clear plans.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: I decided to give up my childhood dreams
I came to know what I truly wanted
I realized that my talents were limited
I stopped asking myself difficult questions

det.korean: 더 중요한 건, 내가 진정으로 원하는 것을 알게 되었다! 어린 시절 작가, 작곡가, 라디오 진행자가 되고 싶던 꿈이 생각났다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① I came to know what I truly wanted
❌ ② I decided to give up my childhood dreams
❌ ③ I realized that my talents were limited
❌ ④ I stopped asking myself difficult questions
✅ I came to know what I truly wanted: 질문에 답하며 자신의 필요/가치를 알게 된 후, 진정한 소망을 깨달음. 이후 어린 시절 꿈을 기억하는 흐름과 일치. ❌ give up dreams: 이후 꿈을 기억하는 맥락과 모순. ❌ talents were limited: 부정적이고 이후 성공 맥락과 불일치. ❌ stopped asking: 질문을 계속하는 맥락과 반대.
det.tip: come to know = '알게 되다'. 빈칸 전후 맥락: 자기 탐색 → 진정한 소망 깨달음 → 어린 시절 꿈 상기 → 계획 구체화.
